name: ChEBI
rationale: Identity authority for chemical structures, and since 2026-08-30 the source of mode_of_action as well: ChEBI asserts mechanism-shaped roles on the same compounds, and conf/sources.yaml maps 32 of them — chosen because the role names a mechanism rather than a structural class — to ModeOfActionEnum, giving covered records an initial seeded mode of action where there were none. That is a RESTATEMENT of a role ChEBI asserts, not an inference from chemistry, which is what separates it from the structural-class map tried and reverted in #47. CC BY 4.0 (LICENSE in the SDF directory, ebi.ac.uk/chebi/about), so ChEBI-derived record content is attributable, not public domain. ChEBI also ships a 3-star-only SDF bulk file that excludes ontology classes by construction; our flat-file path filters for both instead.

name: CARD Antibiotic Resistance Ontology
rationale: Antibiotic molecule subtree, resistance determinants and drug targets. aro.obo/aro.owl are CC BY 4.0 — verified against the arpcard/aro LICENSE, GitHub spdx_id CC-BY-4.0, the OBO Foundry registry and CARD's own download page. Redistributable with credit. Note this is the ONTOLOGY only: card.json is under different, restrictive terms (see card-json).

name: PubChem
rationale: Narrow structure fallback for CARD-only molecules: only CIDs CARD already cross-references are fetched. PubChem CIDs are standardized records, not depositor submissions, so a CID's InChIKey can differ from the structure supplied by a depositor. PubChem is also an aggregator whose annotations retain source-specific reuse terms; this adoption does not authorize wholesale annotation ingestion.

name: CARD card.json
rationale: BLOCKED on licence, not on value. CARD's terms prohibit reproduction of non-ontology materials by any commercial organization without written McMaster permission, and the academic clause requires the materials be unmodified and credited — conditions that conflict with both harmonization and CC0. The AMR Gene Family / Drug Class / Resistance Mechanism categories live here and are exactly what the mechanism layer wants, so a waiver request to McMaster is the highest-value unblocking action available. Until then the is_a+participates_in walk over the CC BY 4.0 ontology stands, typing 4530 of 4555 rows.

name: MIBiG
rationale: MIBiG 4.0.1 producer/BGC assertions are seeded from the CC BY 4.0 bulk JSON. The import accepts an active entry when at least one locus carries an experimental compound-to-producer evidence method, converts SMILES to a Standard InChIKey, and joins only one-to-one exact keys. It preserves taxon, BGC, release and record versions, quality, the admitting evidence methods, the expert-review flag, and a MIBiG-listed reference. The published pre-write dry run found 66 matches, 600 ambiguous structures, and 796 out of scope across 1,462 inventory rows, plus 225 admitted compounds dropped before the inventory for want of a structure; bioactivity labels are deliberately ignored. The dry run's ambiguous class is wider than the seeder's because it names connectivity-only near-misses the seeder simply files as out of scope; the seeder's structure gate matches the same 66, of which it publishes 64: two name a producer that identifies no organism and are refused. An earlier release gated on the changelog reviewer field, which is a migration placeholder on 2,988 of 3,013 entries and admitted 24 entries (#203).

name: FDA Drugs@FDA
rationale: The official 2026-08-28 12-table archive now supplies 3611 product-level APPROVED assertions on 210 exact structure records. The importer requires an approved original submission, excludes tentative approvals and combination products, and preserves jurisdiction, application/product, sponsor, approval date, and marketing status. Discontinued is a marketing state, not evidence that approval was withdrawn, so it never becomes WITHDRAWN.

name: FDA GSRS/UNII
rationale: The 2026-08-31 FDA UNII snapshot selects an exact single-ingredient UNII candidate and batched GSRS records supply chemical structures. A name or UNII never proves approval: the importer computes the GSRS Standard InChIKey and writes only one-to-one full-key corpus matches. Connectivity-only salt, stereo, or protonation matches are reported but rejected; GSRS provenance is preserved separately from Drugs@FDA status provenance.

name: BindingDB curated records
rationale: The 2026-09 literature-curated export is seeded through exact reported-and-recomputed Standard InChIKey, primary-citation, quantitative-measurement, NCBI-taxonomy, and assay-context gates. Despite its curated-only label it contains 429 ChEMBL and 260 Taylor Research Group rows; all 689 are rejected by the exact row-level Curation/DataSource marker. The accepted inventory contains 177 measurements, 95 target assertions, and 45 corpus structures. Kd alone supports DIRECT_BINDING_TARGET; Ki, IC50, and EC50 remain MEASURED_TARGET_ASSOCIATION and do not establish organism activity or mode of action.

name: PHI-base AMR export
rationale: The pinned CC BY 4.0 AMR export contributes primary-literature gene-alteration/chemical resistance associations on exact ChEBI-grounded corpus structures. The importer requires a chemical-specific resistance PHIPO term, antimicrobial_interaction, numeric PMID, pathogen NCBI Taxonomy identifier, exact ChEBI identifier, matching chemical label, and unchanged corpus InChIKey. Upstream chemical-label mismatches, non-resistance phenotypes, missing pathogen taxonomy and out-of-scope chemicals are rejected. Associations remain mechanism_type UNKNOWN because the phenotype establishes resistance but not a biochemical route.

name: CRyPTIC Consortium Dataset
rationale: Release 3.4.0 is CC BY 4.0 and contains 660961 DST rows plus 288904 UKMYC phenotype rows. The adopted compact inventory is generated from the pinned DST_MEASUREMENTS.parquet, UKMYC_PHENOTYPES.parquet and DRUG_CODES.csv.gz release files after verifying upstream MD5s. A hand-audited v3.4.0 drug map grounds 29 of 39 CRyPTIC drug codes to exact corpus structures and leaves mixtures, combinations, drug classes, absent structures and ambiguous stereochemical names explicitly ineligible. Twenty-six mapped codes appear in the phenotype tables, producing 858402 eligible activity rows out of 949865 total. The committed data/raw/cryptic_activity.tsv compacts those exact-mapped observations into 4012 grouped rows keyed by release table, drug, raw method, phenotype, quality and MIC shape. The inventory standardizes CRyPTIC MIC strings into mic_value, mic_qualifier and mic_units while retaining raw MIC columns, records row/isolate/site group counts, and seeds grouped ActivityObservation rows with the source Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex label without inventing a species-level taxon CURIE. CRyPTIC-owned activity_spectrum entries are a replaceable source slice so re-seeding can replace stale upstream observations without touching curated activity rows.

name: ChEMBL bioactivities
rationale: Best assay-attached activity source, and it carries CO-ADD's ~100K antimicrobial measurements (src_id 40) with organism, concentration, medium and detection method genuinely attached. But CC BY-SA 3.0 is copyleft: content can be aggregated alongside, never relabelled, and a share-alike obligation would propagate to the whole corpus. Refused for seeding under the corpus's CC BY 4.0 record licence (#27, decided): share-alike would propagate to every downstream user, which CC BY does not. Second trap: a ChEMBL 'parent' is not a guarantee of one component; GetParent leaves genuine mixtures, all-salt records and organometallics unreduced.

name: Stanford HIV Drug Resistance Database
rationale: 461 antiviral records still carry empty resistance_mechanisms because CARD has nothing for viruses; HIVDB is the strongest HIV-specific candidate but HBV/HSV/influenza remain open. A Sierra maintainer answered the official reuse request on 2026-09-05 and identified hivdb/hivfacts as the data surface Sierra uses, released under the public-domain Unlicense; GitHub identifies the hivfacts LICENSE as SPDX Unlicense. That resolves redistribution for hivfacts, not every Stanford HIVDB endpoint or web page. A hand-audited hivfacts drug map pins commit be1c11a5145fea9073fdb71801919d4a34265336, grounds 16 of 28 rows to exact corpus structures, and leaves boosted combinations, ambiguous tenofovir/TDF identity, and missing corpus structures explicitly unmapped. The committed data/raw/hivdb_algorithm_terms.tsv inventory captures 467 exact HIVDB 10.2 XML drug-specific score-rule formula terms as genotype_resistance_score_rules without flattening them into generic biochemical resistance-mechanism labels.

name: NPAtlas
rationale: BLOCKED on licence. npatlas.org/about states verbatim: "The Natural Products Atlas is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-Noncommercial 4.0 International License" (database version 2024_09, checked 2026-08-29). NonCommercial is incompatible with the corpus's CC BY 4.0 record licence — it would restrict every downstream user of this corpus, which CC0 and CC BY 4.0 both refuse to do. Excellent content for a curator to consult; it cannot be seeded. Compare MIBiG, which closes the same gap under CC BY 4.0.

name: CO-ADD
rationale: The official r03.02-2020 complete CSV archive is live and contains inhibition and dose-response rows with SMILES, assay, organism/strain, concentration or response, and units. The archive contains no README or licence. CO-ADD's Privacy & Copyright page reserves all rights, allows copies only for personal non-commercial use, prohibits systematic download/storage, and requires prior written permission for reproduction/transmission; availability of the bulk download does not override those terms. ChEMBL src_id 40 remains separately CC BY-SA 3.0. A request naming the two official CSV files is archived in research/2026-08-31-reuse-terms-outreach.md. REQUEST DRAFTED, NOT SENT; response: none. Blocked unless CO-ADD grants modification and commercial redistribution of its own bulk files and identifies attribution and third-party exclusions.

name: BV-BRC
rationale: AMR phenotypes carry organism, strain, method, evidence and prediction fields, but roughly 93 percent are computational predictions; a later extractor must require evidence=Laboratory Method and reject every computational row. The website, privacy policy, official documentation repository, and MIT-licensed API software do not grant reuse rights for API data; software licensing is not a data licence. REQUEST SENT 2026-08-31 through the official API tracker: https://github.com/BV-BRC/BV-BRC-API/issues/204. Response pending. Remains UNVERIFIED until an authorized answer covers the public genome_amr data content.

name: BacDive
rationale: BacDive's current site footer explicitly links CC BY 4.0 as its Copyright & License statement, permitting modification and commercial redistribution with attribution. The v2 detail API docs expose name-level met_antibiotica antibiotic S/I/R and concentration fields plus met_antibiogram_v2 disk-diffusion fields; the non-writing evaluator now reads v2 /fetch/{bacdive_id} JSON, summarizes those BacDive antibiotic strings and fixed disk-diffusion columns as identity-curation leads only, emits a fillable exact-structure drug map, validates curated map rows against the current BacDive name report plus current corpus Standard InChIKeys, can emit an exact-map-gated activity-row report preserving BacDive IDs, taxon/strain labels, row references, source sections, raw concentrations, disk diameters and media for downstream audit, and can validate existing exact activity reports against current corpus Standard InChIKeys. Exact chemical grounding remains separate curation work, and legacy v1 endpoints stay out of scope because they are frozen at the April 2025 content state. REQUEST SENT 2026-08-31 through the official BacDive API tracker: https://github.com/LeibnizDSMZ/bacdive-api/issues/1. API tracker maintainer response 2026-09-29: API or bulk-download data are licensed under CC BY 4.0, but the maintainer recommended a BacDive website ticket for official confirmation and the tracker issue was closed on 2026-09-30. Terms look compatible, but no data are adopted until DSMZ confirms the scope for API/bulk susceptibility content and identifies any third-party exclusions.

name: DrugCentral
rationale: Approval, indication, route, structure, and target data are valuable for validation, but the database download is CC BY-SA 4.0. ShareAlike is incompatible with seeding derived record content under the corpus's CC BY 4.0 licence. Use FDA data first; keep DrugCentral as curator reference or in a separately licensed sidecar.

name: WHO AWaRe
rationale: Access/Watch/Reserve classification for 258 antibiotics. The AWaRe antibiotic book is CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO, so its NonCommercial and ShareAlike obligations make it unsuitable for seeding into the CC BY 4.0 corpus; use as curator reference or a separately licensed sidecar.

name: WHO ATC/DDD
rationale: ATC is a distinct dataset from AWaRe and needs its own current terms review. Do not transfer the AWaRe licence conclusion to ATC merely because both sit in the WHO ecosystem.

name: ClinicalTrials.gov
rationale: Trial interventions, phase, recruitment status, dates, and NCT identifiers are useful investigational evidence, not regulatory status. Terms require attribution, current data, processing date, and modification disclosure and warn of international and third-party copyrights. Use as cited curator evidence pending legal review; never infer INVESTIGATIONAL from a name mention or completed study alone.

name: WHO antibacterial clinical pipeline
rationale: Expert-curated antibacterial candidates, phases, expected pathogen activity, route, target/mechanism and innovation. The associated 2025 report/data use CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO terms; keep in a non-commercial/share-alike sidecar or curator workflow, not the main CC BY 4.0 corpus.

name: ChEBI entry citations
rationale: Already extracted into a citations column that nothing reads. A ChEBI entry's references support the COMPOUND, not necessarily an antimicrobial claim about it, so seeding them into evidence needs a stated rule first.

name: LOTUS
rationale: CC0 natural-product structure-organism-reference occurrences distributed through Wikidata. Follow MIBiG and measure incremental coverage. An occurrence in a taxon does not necessarily mean biosynthetic production, so populate producer_organisms only when the cited source explicitly supports production; otherwise a separate occurrence field is needed.

name: COCONUT
rationale: COCONUT describes the curated collection as CC0, but its terms also preserve original data-owner rights. A whole-dataset CC0 label is therefore insufficient for aggregated upstream rows. Preserve source-level provenance and exclude rows without compatible source terms before considering adoption.

name: Norine
rationale: Nonribosomal peptides with monomer-level representation. Sharpened by a verified finding: the Standard InChIKey does not recognise some 1,5 keto-enol tautomers as the same compound, cannot express cis/trans in organometallics, and does not support relative stereochemistry — all live risks for macrocyclic peptides, where our identity model keys on exactly that hash.

name: ClassyFire and NPClassifier
rationale: Computed structural classes would give structural_class to the records CARD does not cover. Computed, not asserted, so it needs its own provenance marker.

name: antiSMASH database
rationale: Predicted clusters across sequenced genomes. Predictions are not evidence of production; useful for leads, not for seeding.

name: MEGARes
rationale: Resistance gene database assembled from CARD, ResFinder, AMRFinderPlus and other sources. Mixed upstream terms and substantial overlap make source-level licensing and incremental-coverage analysis mandatory before use.

name: NCBI AMRFinderPlus
rationale: The public-domain 2026-08-07.1 audit compares 1457 reportable AMR families and 8493 catalog alleles against the 2010 ARO determinants already represented. Exact normalized names overlap for 494 families, a strict lower bound rather than an ontology mapping. The catalog adds primary-PMID and class/subclass evidence, but its drug strings are categories or ungrounded names rather than structure identifiers. No row is seeded: a family/class entry does not establish resistance to every individual compound in that class, and name matching cannot satisfy the corpus identity gate.

name: NCBI Pathogen Detection AST
rationale: The 2026-10-03 native AST Browser snapshot contains 505890 observations from 37166 BioSamples across 538 BioProjects and 144 antibiotic labels. scripts/fetch_ncbi_ast.py captures native AST or isolate metadata exports with checksum manifests, unique identifiers, and matching before/after source counts. curation/ncbi_ast_drug_map.tsv now pins 45 exact active-moiety interpretations and 34 explicit exclusions to the AST snapshot; 65 labels remain unmapped. Nine additional labels identify eight neutral structures, while ceftiofur is explicitly excluded because its lexical corpus candidate is a sodium salt. See research/2026-10-03-ncbi-ast-drug-coverage.md. The expanded map reconstructs 254944 candidates, preserves every previous candidate, and introduces no new assay signatures; the repinned assay review accepts 213144 and quarantines 41800. Fresh taxonomy and BioSample snapshots support disjointness by reported taxonomy and 62 source-verified repeated results; full conversion validates 213082 observations with exact compound identities, preserving 124 paired genome contexts and all 18 affected assemblies. The expanded reviewed inventory compresses losslessly to 8924250 bytes under reports/ only. The full production merge/write/reload/render audit now preserves the expanded cohort and pre-existing evidence, verifies unchanged reseeding and every local site target, and passes representative desktop/mobile browser checks including missing categorical calls. See research/2026-10-03-ncbi-ast-expanded-publication.md. The overlap audit now also pins and expands existing non-AST corpus observations, preserves accession-free evidence as an explicit limitation, and reports raw shared-sample leads without automatically excluding assays or projects. The reviewed cohort has no shared BioSamples with that existing record-level evidence; see research/2026-10-03-ncbi-ast-existing-corpus-overlap.md. The following historical numerical audits describe the original 36-exact-label cohort and its former pinned review files, not automatic publication approval of the expanded cohort. The optional --isolate-snapshot path joins source TaxIDs, versioned assemblies and strain labels on exact versioned PDT targets with agreeing sample, project and scientific-name context. The exact report and seeder preserve separate isolate snapshot checksum/date provenance in addition to the original AST source version. Excluding 3203 uninformative-only assay groups leaves 230294 candidates, all with TaxIDs and 226549 with assemblies. The reproducible CRyPTIC audit rebuilds both inventories and finds 1142 shared raw BioSamples but zero candidate sample or project overlaps; alternative accessions and 11370 CRyPTIC phenotype isolates without WGS links remain outside that comparison. The pinned assay-context review covers all 60 candidate signatures, accepts 188811 observations, and quarantines 41483 for unresolved measurement, panel-format, vendor or method context. The seeder requires an accepted exact review decision and preserves its checksum and evidence. No observation is seeded. A checksum-pinned NCBI taxonomy audit places all 433 reviewed TaxIDs outside the CRyPTIC complex, with exact source-name agreement and no direct sample conflict. This addresses alias and phenotype-only overlap for this subset conditional on reported identity and CRyPTIC release scope; it does not independently re-identify isolates or establish within-source uniqueness. Original BioSample antibiograms confirm 52 single submitted results repeated across two targets each. The pinned review consolidates 188811 export groups into 188759 observations while retaining all 104 paired genome contexts and 18 distinct assemblies in the affected rows; distinct assays remain separate. See research/2026-10-03-ncbi-ast-biosample-consolidation.md. The non-publishing production-path audit now verifies all 188759 observations across 32 records through merge, closed-schema YAML writing, full reload equality, unchanged reseeding, and rendered activity-cell comparison; all unaffected records remain unchanged. The dated report retains the snapshot-specific count. The affected artifacts total 561498455 YAML bytes and 120919520 HTML bytes before the inherited table-accessibility wrapper update, exposing a lossless storage and bounded browsing requirement (#1022). See research/2026-10-03-ncbi-ast-publication-audit.md. The follow-up lossless-collection audit retains complete expanded records and reduces total record storage to 24863430 bytes; see research/2026-10-03-ncbi-ast-activity-collections.md. The bounded-publication audit now verifies all activity pages, search-index bindings and complete expanded-record downloads, with full-site local-link and desktop/mobile browser checks; see research/2026-10-03-ncbi-ast-bounded-publication.md. The compressed source inventory preserves the exact report bytes and every reviewed observation, with separate stored-file and expanded-content provenance checks; see research/2026-10-03-ncbi-ast-compressed-inventory.md. Adoption still needs the deferred source-terms decision, source configuration, committed inventory/provenance entry, and publication gates; quarantined contexts and unmapped antibiotics remain curation work. See research/2026-10-03-ncbi-ast-taxonomic-overlap.md. See research/2026-10-03-ncbi-ast-assay-review.md and the preceding snapshot/enrichment/adoption-audit reports. Native AST PDT values are not genome accessions.

name: CDC/FDA AR Isolate Bank
rationale: Public isolate product pages expose isolate-specific organism labels, BioSample links, reference broth microdilution MIC tables and CLSI interpretation notes as stable manual citations. CDC's Use of Agency Materials says most CDC and ATSDR website information is public domain and may be freely used or reproduced with agency attribution; AR Bank product sheets also bind shipped cultures to the SLA and say the materials may not be redistributed. Treat that restriction as applying to biological materials: do not redistribute cultures, do not seed a scraped panel inventory, and use individual public product pages only as cited CURATE_ONLY evidence for hand-reviewed MIC rows until CDC/FDA confirms a bulk AST-data licence.

name: RCSB Protein Data Bank
rationale: The CC0 API audit queries the compounds carrying 95 established BindingDB targets, requiring both an exact Standard InChIKey and an existing target UniProt accession. It finds 42 candidate PDB entries across 8 records and preserves PDB plus primary citation metadata. No evidence is seeded yet: entry-level ligand/protein co-occurrence does not prove atomic contact, and repeated BindingDB variant labels inflate the 243 raw target-entry pairs. Adoption requires component-specific ligand-to-polymer contact validation and deduplication to the stable target identity.

name: DrugBank
rationale: Excellent data, but the licence does not permit redistribution in a CC0 knowledge base. Usable as a curator reference only, never seeded. Terms NOT verified against the source's own licence page by this repository — the restrictive reading is widely known but unchecked here, so the row stays UNVERIFIED and BLOCKED rather than claiming a determination nobody made.

name: KEGG DRUG
rationale: Same shape of problem as DrugBank: freely readable, not freely redistributable. ChEBI already carries kegg.compound and kegg.drug cross-references, which is the useful half. Terms NOT verified against the source's own licence page by this repository — the restrictive reading is widely known but unchecked here, so the row stays UNVERIFIED and BLOCKED rather than claiming a determination nobody made.

name: CLSI breakpoint standards
rationale: Paywalled standards documents. A curator may consult them; the corpus cannot carry them. Terms NOT verified against the source's own licence page by this repository — the restrictive reading is widely known but unchecked here, so the row stays UNVERIFIED and BLOCKED rather than claiming a determination nobody made.

name: EUCAST breakpoint tables
rationale: Current XLS/PDF tables provide versioned clinical interpretation thresholds, not measured MIC observations. EUCAST allows reuse with attribution but prohibits resale, which is incompatible with unrestricted commercial redistribution of the corpus. Keep in a versioned standards sidecar or curator tooling.

name: Discovery and review literature
rationale: Present so the gap is visible rather than absent. causal_graphs is 0% and is the thing this repository exists to hold, but it is not ingestible from any database: a mechanism graph is curator-authored from primary literature, one compound at a time, with every edge carrying its own citation. Listed as REFERENCE to record that no source will close this column and the work belongs in NEXT_TASKS, not here.
